segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: One secondary school will move its first lesson from eight fifteen to nine o'clock for a one-term trial. The change follows complaints from students about early transport and tiredness.

segments.speaker: Principal
segments.text: We are not assuming a later start automatically improves learning. We want to measure attendance, lateness, concentration and after-school participation before deciding whether the timetable should change permanently.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: Some parents welcome the trial, but others say a later finish could interfere with sports, part-time jobs and family routines.

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: I like the idea because my bus leaves before seven. But if clubs finish later, I could get home after six. The benefit in the morning might simply move the problem to the evening.

segments.speaker: Reporter
segments.text: The school has therefore kept Friday clubs at their existing time and will survey families halfway through the term rather than waiting until the end.

options: A later start to the first lesson
questions.explanationJa: first lessonを8:15から9:00へ遅らせます。

questions.prompt: Give two measures the principal wants to examine.
What concern does the student raise?
options: The school bus may become free.
A later finish may shift the difficulty from morning to evening.
The trial is too short to notice.
questions.explanationJa: morningのbenefitがeveningの遅さに移るだけかもしれないと指摘します。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO activities or routines that could be affected by a later finish.
questions.explanationJa: sportsとpart-time jobsが具体的に挙げられます。

questions.prompt: The school will survey families ________ through the term.
questions.explanationJa: term終了まで待たずhalfwayでsurveyします。

questions.prompt: What does the report emphasize about the trial?
options: The result has already been decided.
Several benefits and costs will be measured before a permanent decision.
The timetable will never change again.
questions.explanationJa: 複数のeffectを測定してからpermanent decisionを行うtrialです。

title: Who should use the community fridge?

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: A neighbourhood centre has opened a community fridge where local shops and residents can leave safe surplus food. Coordinator Maya Singh, who is allowed to take food?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Anyone. We deliberately avoid asking people to prove financial need. A complicated check might reduce misuse, but it could also discourage someone who needs help from using the service.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: Does open access create problems?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Sometimes one person takes a large amount. We respond by posting simple guidance about sharing rather than policing every item. The bigger challenge is food safety. Volunteers record delivery times and remove food that should not be kept.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: What do local shops gain from participating?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: They reduce waste, but they also need clear rules. Staff need to know what can be donated and how quickly it must reach us. Good intentions do not replace a reliable system.

segments.speaker: Interviewer
segments.text: So the project tries to balance dignity, access and safety.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Exactly. If the system protects food but embarrasses users, it has failed socially. If it welcomes everyone but ignores safety, it has failed practically.

questions.prompt: Who may take food from the fridge?
questions.explanationJa: financial proofを求めずanyoneが利用できます。

questions.prompt: Why does Maya avoid a formal needs check? Give two linked ideas.
markscheme: But it could discourage or embarrass people who genuinely need help.
questions.explanationJa: misuse対策にはなっても、needのある人を遠ざける可能性があります。

questions.prompt: How does the project respond when one person takes a large amount?
options: It posts guidance about sharing rather than checking every item.
questions.explanationJa: strict policingではなくsharing guidanceを使います。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO food-safety or operational practices mentioned.
options: Removing food that should not be kept
questions.explanationJa: delivery time記録とunsafe foodのremoveが重要です。

questions.prompt: Maya says good intentions do not replace a reliable ________.
questions.explanationJa: good intentionsだけではなくreliable systemが必要です。

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Our final topic is whether secondary students should complete a minimum number of community-service hours before graduation. Teacher Daniel Reed supports the idea.

segments.speaker: Reed
segments.text: Schools teach citizenship in classrooms, but service lets students see how local organizations actually work. A requirement also ensures that volunteering is not limited to students who already have family connections to opportunities.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Student advocate Sara Khan, you oppose making it compulsory.

segments.speaker: Sara
segments.text: I support volunteering. I object to pretending every student has the same free time. Some care for siblings, work paid jobs or travel long distances. A fixed requirement can punish the students whose responsibilities are already greatest.

segments.speaker: Reed
segments.text: Then the school should provide options during school hours and recognize different forms of contribution, including caring responsibilities where appropriate. The solution is to design the requirement fairly, not abandon it.

segments.speaker: Sara
segments.text: That helps, but motivation matters too. If students count every minute only because they need a certificate, organizations may spend more time supervising reluctant volunteers than receiving useful help.

segments.speaker: Moderator
segments.text: Is there any common ground?

segments.speaker: Reed
segments.text: Schools should definitely make opportunities easier to access.

segments.speaker: Sara
segments.text: I agree with that. We disagree about whether participation should be mandatory.

questions.prompt: What is one argument Reed gives for a requirement?
options: It gives students practical experience of local organizations.
questions.explanationJa: citizenshipをlocal organizationで実際に経験できる点を挙げます。

questions.prompt: Give two responsibilities Sara says can limit students' free time.
markscheme: Caring for siblings and/or other caring responsibilities.
Paid work and/or long travel times.
questions.explanationJa: sibling care、paid job、long travelなどです。

questions.prompt: How does Reed respond to the fairness concern?
options: He says all students have equal time.
He suggests school-time options and recognition of different contributions.
He wants to increase the required hours.
questions.explanationJa: school hours内のoptionやdifferent contributionのrecognitionを提案します。

questions.prompt: Choose TWO concerns or conditions discussed.
options: Access to opportunities should be easier.
Reluctant volunteers may create extra supervision work.
questions.explanationJa: access改善とreluctant volunteerのsupervision負担が論点です。

questions.prompt: Matching task: Match each speaker to the position they emphasize: Reed and Sara.
markscheme: Reed — a fair requirement can broaden access and provide civic experience.
Sara — volunteering should be supported, but compulsory hours may ignore unequal responsibilities and motivation.
questions.explanationJa: Reedはfair requirement、Saraはmandatory化の問題を強調します。

questions.prompt: What common ground do the speakers reach?
options: Schools should make volunteering opportunities easier to access.
Community service should be removed from schools.
questions.explanationJa: opportunityへのaccess改善には両者が同意しています。
